spec.title: User-local stewardship state and capability profiles

home.title: 1. State home

p.STATE-HOME: The state root, the **steward home**, is `<settings dir>/steward/`, where the settings directory is `$VIBE_SETTINGS` when that variable is set and non-empty and `~/.vibe` otherwise. It belongs to one person and may be shared by that person's successive central agents. It is not committed, packaged, mirrored or treated as another contributor's authority.

p.HOME-OVERRIDE: Every packaged script that locates the steward home resolves it through the one shared helper `skills/steward-common/scripts/steward_home.py` and accepts `--home` as an explicit override: `resolve_context.py`, and `render_goal.py` and `render_tree.py` when run with `--resolve`. `bind_context.py` takes the home from its `--context` directory, which must lie in that home's `contexts/` directory. No other environment variable selects the home.

home.fence: <settings dir>/steward/ config.toml contexts/ <opaque-context-id>/ binding.toml settings.toml plan.toml GOAL.md GOAL-CLAUDE.txt custody.toml view/ sessions/ handoffs/ records/

p.OPTIONAL-CONTINUITY-RECORDS: The binding, settings, complete plan and repository tree are sufficient for ordinary continuation. `sessions/`, `handoffs/` and `records/` are optional diagnostic or explicit-formal-workflow material; a timeout, crash, compaction, new chat or model/account change, quota exhaustion or provider overload does not require creating or receiving any of them. Optional recovery evidence can use existing record/evidence surfaces without changing schema 1.

p.PROVIDER-IDENTITY-IS-NOT-CONTEXT: A provider account is not a stewardship identity or binding key. An owner-initiated account change on the same OS user and exact checkout resumes the existing context; changing OS user or machine does not authorize reading another user's private state. Never store credentials or secrets in plans, goals, packets or recovery reports. Availability and retry observations belong in local evidence, not in shared project policy.

p.OPAQUE-CONTEXT-ID: `opaque-context-id` is a random UUID rendered as lowercase ASCII. It is an identity only; never parse meaning from it. The context directory is named by its id, and a binding whose `context_id` differs from that name is invalid and reported. Discovery scans `contexts/*/binding.toml`, so no mutable global context index is required.

p.HOME-IS-THE-ONLY-PLANNING-TRUTH: Nothing outside the steward home is a planning source of truth for a context. Generated files elsewhere, exported pages and dashboards are copies; a second plan for the same project outside the context's `plan.toml` is not allowed.

p.VIEW-IS-DISPOSABLE: `view/` holds the derived tree view of the context's plan (`index.html`, `plan-tree.json`). It may be deleted at any time, is never read back as state, and is regenerated from `plan.toml` on demand.

p.HOME-IS-PORTABLE: The whole steward home may be copied to another of the same person's machines at any time and works there without repair: context resolution uses repository identity and never reads recorded paths. Concurrent writers on two machines are not coordinated; the person keeps one machine writing at a time.

p.CREATE-DEFAULTS: An owner-facing central session that finds no `config.toml` creates it before campaign work with the safe defaults below. Package installation itself never writes user state.

p.CONFIG-STRICT: The file is strict human-authored TOML. Unknown top-level keys are rejected and surfaced; they are not silently ignored. It is operator configuration, so JTD is intentionally out of scope.

binding.title: 3. Context binding

p.BINDING-TUPLE: A schema-1 binding (the previous format, still read) binds an exact tuple: canonical repository root, canonical worktree root, Git common directory, and branch ref (or detached commit). It matches only that exact tuple, so moving or copying the checkout loses the match until the binding is converted to schema 2.

binding.fence: schema = 1 context_id = "3d7a79bf-5f27-4b88-9eaa-c8323df5cb03" project_name = "example" repository_root = "C:/work/example" worktree_root = "C:/work/example" git_common_dir = "C:/work/example/.git" revision_selector = "refs/heads/main"

p.REPOSITORY-IDENTITY: A project is identified by its repository, not by a path: `repository_id` is the lexicographically smallest root commit id reachable from `HEAD` (`git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD`). Every clone and worktree of one repository yields the same id on every machine. A shallow clone has no usable identity, because its boundary commits look like roots, and it is refused until it is unshallowed.

p.BINDING-SCHEMA-2: A schema-2 binding names the repository by `repository_id`. `default = true` marks the context used when several contexts share that repository and none serves the current branch; at most one context per `repository_id` holds it. `revisions` optionally lists the branch selectors (`main` or `refs/heads/main`) this context serves; empty means any. Several checkouts and roles of one project therefore share one context and one plan.

binding.fence:
schema = 2 context_id = "3d7a79bf-5f27-4b88-9eaa-c8323df5cb03" project_name = "example" repository_id = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567" default = true revisions = []
[[seen]] worktree_root = "C:/work/example"

p.CONTEXT-RESOLUTION: Resolution order is: (1) a context id named by the owner; (2) the schema-2 contexts whose `repository_id` equals the current repository's: exactly one wins; among several, the one whose `revisions` contains the current branch wins, else the one with `default = true`; otherwise resolution refuses and lists the candidates; (3) a schema-1 binding whose exact path tuple matches; (4) otherwise "no context". Resolution never guesses, never settles a tie by timestamp and never creates or repairs a context; creating a context and writing a binding are separate explicit actions. Once resolved, any owner-facing central agent may continue from that context under the current owner instruction; a previous holder/session claim is not authority.

p.RESOLVER-TOOLS: The reference resolver is `skills/steward-common/scripts/resolve_context.py`: read-only, JSON output, exit 0 found, 1 none, 2 ambiguous, 3 error. `bind_context.py` in the same directory writes a schema-2 binding for an existing context only on explicit request: it converts schema 1 by keeping `context_id` and `project_name`, computing `repository_id` and moving the old path tuple into one `[[seen]]` entry, and it refuses a second `default = true` for one repository unless told `--take-default`, which moves the default.

settings.title: 4. Settings and live switching

p.SETTING-PRECEDENCE: Effective settings use this precedence: current owner instruction > current-context `settings.toml` > global `config.toml` > safe defaults. An owner instruction such as “switch the planning mode to ultra” updates the current context file immediately and applies within the same session; no `vibe` command or restart is required.

settings.fence: schema = 1 interaction_mode = "auto" planning_profile = "ultra" goal_node = "COMPILER-MODERNIZATION" updated_at = "2026-08-29T11:00:00Z" updated_by = "owner-chat"

p.SETTINGS-ORTHOGONAL: `interaction_mode` (`auto | collab`) controls how much the central coordinator narrates and asks. `planning_profile` (`ultra | standard`) controls planning scaffolding. `goal_node` selects the stable campaign/root node whose goal is projected; it is required whenever selection is not unique. The axes are independent. Historic input aliases `normal` and `medium` normalize to `standard`; stored values are canonical.

td.PROFILE-ATOM-ULTRA: May span a coherent high-context cell when acceptance stays reviewable

td.PROFILE-EXPANSION-ULTRA: May retain more hierarchy in reasoning; still persists the full route and current frontier

td.PROFILE-EXPANSION-STANDARD: Persist explicit substeps, dependencies and per-node acceptance before execution

td.PROFILE-BACKSCAN-ULTRA: Milestones, handoffs, architecture changes and closure

td.PROFILE-BACKSCAN-STANDARD: Those boundaries plus every completed parent node

td.PROFILE-REVIEW-ULTRA: Independent review selected by risk and verifiability

td.PROFILE-REVIEW-STANDARD: Independent review preferred for broad judgment or public boundaries

td.PROFILE-FAILURE-ULTRA: May replan a wider region at once

td.PROFILE-FAILURE-STANDARD: Stop the current atom, record evidence, refine the next small region

p.PROFILE-CANNOT-WAIVE: No profile may waive owner authority, destructive-action fences, lossless requirement coverage, central review, exact gates or fact promotion. When the owner explicitly requests a formal handoff, no profile may waive its receipt.

p.SESSION-ID: A central agent may choose a fresh opaque `session_id` and write a uniquely named record under `sessions/` for diagnostics. The optional record names harness, model as observed metadata, effective profile, start time and observed custody epoch. Neither the id nor the record is required to resume or continue, and neither grants authority. Model identity informs forensics; it never selects the profile automatically.

p.NO-SECRETS: Local records may carry absolute paths but never tokens, API keys, Authorization values, raw sensitive provider bodies or copied environment dumps. Record a secret source name or token-file path only when operationally necessary.

p.GENERATED-HAS-NO-PATHS: Generated files (`GOAL.md`, `GOAL-CLAUDE.txt`, the tree view) embed no absolute path, so a copied steward home carries no stale machine path in them.
